Alice — thanks for the 30m earlier. Quick recap and a small set of asks so we can size the right onboarding path. TL;DR: we can support both Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, single-tenant compute) and Private (VPC / on-prem) — each maps to different operational responsibilities and evidence you asked for.

Recap of what you said on the call:
- Data residency: all inference inputs and outputs must remain in your AWS account/region.
- No shared compute: you prefer single-tenant GPU pools or on-prem if possible.
- Key management: BYOK or HSM is required for secrets and model keys.
- Auditability: retention of request logs and KV cache eviction events for 12 months.

What I need from you to tighten our recommendation:
1) Confirm whether you require the control plane to be customer-managed (i.e., Private deployment) or if a private Dedicated offering (Redwood-managed control plane + dedicated compute in our tenancy) is acceptable.
2) A prioritized list of the compliance artifacts you need first (SOC2 report, architecture diagram, KMS integration guide, deployment runbook, penetration test summary).
3) Preferred POC timeline (we proposed 6 weeks on the call; tell me if you need longer).

Next steps I propose:
- If you want rapid validation: start with Dedicated capacity (we can provision single-tenant GPU pools in your region, BYOK for control-plane secrets, and provide the custody evidence pack) — typical POC 4–6 weeks.
- If you need control-plane residency or air gap: we’ll move to Private (VPC or on-prem). That needs additional implementation work and an SOW; POC 8–12+ weeks depending on network approvals.

I attached the copy of the security worksheet you shared during the call (see attachment). Ben, flag anything I missed from the solutions/ops side.

Attachments: security_requirements_v2.pdf (from HealthScope)

Thanks — happy to sync again once you confirm the three asks above.
